Than
creator: A. Arman, A. Bondarenko, A. Prymak, D. Radchenko
description: Abstract . For every n ≥ 2 n\geq 2 , we construct a body U n U_{n} of constant width 2 2 in 𝔼 n {\mathbb{E}}^{n} with small volume and symmetries of a regular n n -simplex. U 2 U_{2} is the Reuleaux triangle.

title: Mixture of Experts in a Mixture of RL settings
creator: Timon Willi, Johan Obando-Ceron, Jakob Foerster, Karolina Dziugaite, Pablo Samuel Castro, Foerster Lab for AI Research, University of Oxford, Mila - Québec AI Institute, Université de Montréal, McGill University, Google DeepMind
description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Timon Willi, Johan Obando-Ceron, Jakob Foerster, Karolina Dziugaite, Pablo Samuel Castro, Foerster Lab for AI Research, University of Oxford, Mila - Québec AI Institute, Université de Montréal, McGill University, Google DeepMind. Mixtures of Experts (MoEs) have gained prominence in (self-)supervised learning due to their enhanced inference efficiency, adaptability to distributed training, and modularity.

title: Differential error feedback for communication-efficient decentralized learning Thanks: A short conference version of this work appears in [ 1 ] . This extended version includes proofs, derivations, and new results. R. Nassif is with Université Côte d’Azur, I3S Laboratory, CNRS, France (email: roula.
creator: Roula Nassif, Stefan Vlaski, Marco Carpentiero
description: Abstract Communication-constrained algorithms for decentralized learning and optimization rely on local updates coupled with the exchange of compressed signals. In this context, differential quantization is an effective technique to mitigate the negative impact of compression by leveraging correlations between successive iterates.

title: Repeat and Concatenate: 2D to 3D Image Translation with 3D to 3D Generative Modeling
creator: Abril Corona-Figueroa, Hubert P. H. Shum, Chris G. Willcocks
description: Abstract This paper investigates a 2D to 3D image translation method with a straightforward technique, enabling correlated 2D X-ray to 3D CT-like reconstruction. We observe that existing approaches, which integrate information across multiple 2D views in the latent space, lose valuable signal information during latent encoding.

title: Upper Bounds on the Mass of Fundamental Fields from Primordial Universe
creator: Hassan Firouzjahi
description: Abstract We study the fluctuations in the vacuum zero point energy associated to quantum fields and their statistical distributions during inflation. It is shown that the perturbations in the vacuum zero point energy have large amplitudes which are highly non-Gaussian. The effects of vacuum zero point fluctuations can be interpreted as the loop corrections in primordial power spectrum and bispectrum.

title: Theories of flavour from the Planck scale to the electroweak scale
description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by . The flavour puzzle remains as one of the most intriguing enigmas of particle physics. A priori , there is no apparent reason for the existence of three identical families of fundamental fermions in Nature.

title: Non-Markovian Quantum Exceptional Points
creator: Jhen-Dong Lin, Po-Chen Kuo, Neill Lambert, Adam Miranowicz, Franco Nori, Yueh-Nan Chen
description: Abstract Exceptional points (EPs) are singularities in the spectra of non-Hermitian operators, where eigenvalues and eigenvectors coalesce. Recently, open quantum systems have been increasingly explored as EP testbeds due to their natural non-Hermitian nature. However, existing works mostly focus on the Markovian limit, leaving a gap in understanding EPs in the non-Markovian regime.

title: On Approximate 8-bit Floating-Point Operations Using Integer Operations Thanks: This work was financed by the ELLIIT strategic research environment through the project D3 ACRE – Approximate Computing Reducing Energy.
creator: 1 st Theodor Lindberg, 2 nd Oscar Gustafsson
description: Abstract In this work, approximate eight-bit floating-point operations performed using simple integer operations is discussed. For two-bit mantissa formats, faithful rounding can always be obtained for the considered operations. For all operations, correctly rounded results can be obtained for different rounding modes, either directly or by adding a conditional carry in.

title: Sum-of-Squares Lower Bounds for Independent Set in Ultra-Sparse Random Graphs
creator: Pravesh K. Kothari, Aaron Potechin, Jeff Xu
description: Abstract We prove that for every D ∈ ℕ D\in\mathbb{N} , and large enough constant d ∈ ℕ d\in\mathbb{N} , with high probability over the choice of G ∼ G ⁡ ( n , d / n ) G\sim G(n,d/n) , the Erdős-Rényi random graph distribution, the canonical degree 2 ​ D 2D Sum-of-Squares relaxation fails to certify that the

title: Detecting Brittle Decisions for Free: Leveraging Margin Consistency in Deep Robust Classifiers
creator: Jonas Ngnawé, Sabyasachi Sahoo, Yann Pequignot, Frédéric Precioso, Christian Gagné
description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jonas Ngnawé, Sabyasachi Sahoo, Yann Pequignot, Frédéric Precioso, Christian Gagné. Despite extensive research on adversarial training strategies to improve robustness, the decisions of even the most robust deep learning models can still be quite sensitive to imperceptible perturbations, creating serious risks when deploying them for high-stakes real-world applications. While detecting such cases may be critical, evaluating a model’s vulnerability at a per-instance level using adversarial attacks is computationally too intensive and unsuitable for real-time deployment scenarios.

title: Scalable tomography of many-body quantum environments with low temporal entanglement
creator: Ilia A. Luchnikov, Michael Sonnner, Dmitry A. Abanin
description: Abstract Describing dynamics of a quantum system coupled to a complex many-body environment is a ubiquitous problem in quantum science. General non-Markovian environments are characterized by their influence matrix (IM) – a multi-time tensor arising from repeated interactions between the system and environment.

title: KAGNNs: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks meet Graph Learning
creator: Roman Bresson, Giannis Nikolentzos, George Panagopoulos, Michail Chatzianastasis, Jun Pang, Michalis Vazirgiannis
description: Abstract In recent years, Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have become the de facto tool for learning node and graph representations. Most GNNs typically consist of a sequence of neighborhood aggregation (a.k.a., message-passing) layers, within which the representation of each node is updated based on those of its neighbors.

title: Blockchain Based Zero-Knowledge Proof of Location in IoT Thanks: This work is supported in part by the grants from the National Science Foundation of China (No. 61571330), Shanghai Integrated Military and Cilivian Development Fund (No. JMRH-2018-1075), and Science and Technology Commission of Shangh
creator: Wei Wu, Erwu Liu, Xinglin Gong and Rui Wang
description: Abstract With the development of precise positioning technology, a growing number of location-based services (LBSs) facilitate people’s life. Most LBSs require proof of location (PoL) to prove that the user satisfies the service requirement, which exposes the user’s privacy. In this paper, we propose a zero-knowledge proof of location (zk-PoL) protocol to better protect the user’s privacy.

title: Broadening the Canonical Picture of EUV-Driven Photoevaporation of Accretion Disks Numpy ( Harris et al. 2020 ) , Matplotlib ( Hunter 2007 ) , Astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2022 ) , SciPy ( Virtanen et al. 2020 )
creator: Riouhei Nakatani, Neal J. Turner, Shinsuke Takasao
description: Abstract Photoevaporation driven by hydrogen-ionizing radiation, also known as extreme-ultraviolet (EUV), profoundly shapes the lives of diverse astrophysical objects. Focusing here mainly on the dispersal of protoplanetary disks, we construct an analytical model accounting for the finite timescales of photoheating and photoionization.

title: Categorification of quantum Borcherds-Bozec algebras Thanks: ∗ Corresponding author.
creator: Stefano V. Kang, Young Rock Kim ∗, Bolun Tong
description: Abstract . We categorify the quantum Borcherds-Bozec algebra U q ​ ( 𝔤 ) U_{q}(\mathfrak{g}) for an arbitrary Borcherds-Cartan datum by constructing their associated Khovanov-Lauda-Rouquier algebras. In the Jordan quiver case, we show that the cyclotomic Khovanov-Lauda-Rouquier algebras provide a categorification of the irreducible highest weight U q ​ ( 𝔤 ) U_{q}(\mathfrak{g}) -modules.

title: On the increase of the melting temperature of water confined in one-dimensional nano-cavities
creator: Flaviano Della Pia, Andrea Zen, Venkat Kapil, Fabian L. Thiemann, Dario Alfè, Angelos Michaelides
description: Abstract Water confined in nanoscale cavities plays a crucial role in everyday phenomena in geology and biology, as well as technological applications at the water-energy nexus. However, even understanding the basic properties of nano-confined water is extremely challenging for theory, simulations, and experiments.

title: Alchemical insights into approximately quadratic energies of iso-electronic atoms
creator: Simon León Krug, O. Anatole von Lilienfeld
description: Abstract Accurate quantum mechanics based predictions of property trends are so important for materials design and discovery that even inexpensive approximate methods are valuable. We use the Alchemical Integral Transform (AIT) to study multi-electron atoms, and to gain a better understanding of the approximately quadratic behavior of energy differences between iso-electronic atoms in their nuclear charges.

title: Equilibria in a Hypercube Spatial Voting Model
creator: A. Nicholas Day, J. Robert Johnson
description: Abstract We give conditions for equilibria in the following Voronoi game on the discrete hypercube. Two players position themselves in { 0 , 1 } d \{0,1\}^{d} and each receives payoff equal to the measure (under some probability distribution) of their Voronoi cell (the set of all points which are closer to them than to the other player).

title: Preference Elicitation for Offline Reinforcement Learning
creator: Alizée Pace, Bernhard Schölkopf, Gunnar Rätsch, Giorgia Ramponi
description: Abstract Applying reinforcement learning (RL) to real-world problems is often made challenging by the inability to interact with the environment and the difficulty of designing reward functions. Offline RL addresses the first challenge by considering access to an offline dataset of environment interactions labeled by the reward function.

title: Hook length biases for self-conjugate partitions and partitions with distinct odd parts
creator: Catherine H. Cossaboom
description: Abstract . We establish a hook length bias between self-conjugate partitions and partitions of distinct odd parts, demonstrating that there are more hooks of fixed length t ≥ 2 t\geq 2 among self-conjugate partitions of n n than among partitions of distinct odd parts of n n for sufficiently large n n .

title: Parameter selection and optimization of a computational network model of blood flow in single-ventricle patients Journal: rsif
creator: Alyssa M Taylor-LaPole 1, L. Mihaela Paun 2, Dan Lior 3, Justin D Weigand 3, Charles Puelz 3, Mette S Olufsen 1
description: Abstract Hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS) is a congenital heart disease responsible for 23% of infant cardiac deaths each year in the United States . HLHS patients are born with an underdeveloped left heart, requiring several surgeries to reconstruct the aorta and create a single ventricle circuit known as the Fontan circulation.

title: WildGuard : Open One-stop Moderation Tools for Safety Risks, Jailbreaks, and Refusals of LLMs
creator: Seungju Han, Kavel Rao, Allyson Ettinger, Liwei Jiang, Bill Yuchen Lin, Nathan Lambert, Yejin Choi, Nouha Dziri
description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Seungju Han, Kavel Rao, Allyson Ettinger, Liwei Jiang, Bill Yuchen Lin, Nathan Lambert, Yejin Choi, Nouha Dziri. We introduce WildGuard —an open, light-weight moderation tool for LLM safety that achieves three goals: (1) identifying malicious intent in user prompts, (2) detecting safety risks of model responses, and (3) determining model refusal rate. Together, WildGuard serves the increasing needs for automatic safety moderation and evaluation of LLM interactions, providing a one-stop tool with enhanced accuracy and broad coverage across 13 risk categories.

title: White dwarf constraints on geological processes at the population level
creator: Andrew M. Buchan, Amy Bonsor, Laura K. Rogers, Marc G. Brouwers, Oliver Shorttle, Pier-Emmanuel Tremblay
description: Abstract White dwarf atmospheres are frequently polluted by material from their own planetary systems. Absorption features from Ca, Mg, Fe and other elements can provide unique insights into the provenance of this exoplanetary material, with their relative abundances being used to infer accretion of material with core- or mantle-like composition.

title: ViPErLEED package II: Spot tracking, extraction and processing of I ( V ) curves
creator: Michael Schmid, Florian Kraushofer, Alexander M. Imre, Tilman Kißlinger, Lutz Hammer, Ulrike Diebold, Michele Riva
description: Abstract As part of the ViPErLEED project (Vienna package for Erlangen LEED, low-energy electron diffraction), computer programs have been developed for facile and user-friendly data extraction from movies of LEED images. The programs make use of some concepts from astronomical image processing and analysis.

title: System for Measurement of Electric Energy Using Beacons with Optical Sensors and LoRaWAN Transmission Thanks: This work was supported by the National Centre for Research and Development within the Smart Growth Operational Programme (agreement No. POIR.01.02.00-00-0352/16-00).
creator: Łukasz Marcul and Mateusz Brzozowski, Artur Janicki
description: Abstract In this article, we present the results of experiments with finding an efficient radio transmission method for an electric energy measurement system called OneMeter 2.0. This system offers a way of collecting energy usage data from beacons attached to regular, non-smart meters.

title: LoongTrain: Efficient Training of Long-Sequence LLMs with Head-Context Parallelism
creator: Diandian Gu, Peng Sun, Qinghao Hu, Ting Huang, Xun Chen, Yingtong Xiong, Guoteng Wang, Qiaoling Chen, Shangchun Zhao, Jiarui Fang, Yonggang Wen, Tianwei Zhang, Xin Jin, Xuanzhe Liu
description: Abstract . Efficiently training LLMs with long sequences is important yet challenged by the massive computation and memory requirements. Sequence parallelism has been proposed to tackle these problems, but existing methods suffer from scalability or efficiency issues. We propose LoongTrain, a novel system to efficiently train LLMs with long sequences at scale.

title: Universal Anomaly Detection at the LHC: Transforming Optimal Classifiers and the DDD Method
creator: Sascha Caron, José Enrique García Navarro, María Moreno Llácer, Polina Moskvitina, Mats Rovers, Adrián Rubio Jímenez, Roberto Ruiz de Austri, Zhongyi Zhang
description: Abstract In this work, we present a novel approach to transform supervised classifiers into effective unsupervised anomaly detectors. The method we have developed, termed Discriminatory Detection of Distortions (DDD), enhances anomaly detection by training a discriminator model on both original and artificially modified datasets.

title: A 3 mm Spectral Line Study of the Central Molecular Zone Infrared Dark Cloud G1.75-0.08
creator: Oskari Miettinen, Miguel Santander-García
description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Oskari Miettinen, Miguel Santander-García. Infrared dark clouds (IRDCs) are fruitful objects to study the fragmentation of interstellar filaments and initial conditions and early stages of high-mass ( M > 8 M>8 M ⊙ ) star formation. We used the Yebes 40 m and Institut de Radioastronomie Millimétrique (IRAM) 30 m radio telescopes to carry out the first single-pointing spectral line observations towards the IRDC G1.75-0.08, which is a filamentary Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) cloud.

title: Green / WeakCoupling : Implementation of fully self-consistent finite-temperature many-body perturbation theory for molecules and solids
creator: Sergei Iskakov, Chia-Nan Yeh, Pavel Pokhilko, Yang Yu, Lei Zhang, Gaurav Harsha, Vibin Abraham, Ming Wen, Munkhorgil Wang, Jacob Adamski, Tianran Chen, Emanuel Gull, Dominika Zgid
description: Abstract The accurate ab-initio simulation of molecules and periodic solids with diagrammatic perturbation theory is an important task in quantum chemistry, condensed matter physics, and materials science. In this article, we present the WeakCoupling module of the open-source software package Green , which implements fully self-consistent diagrammatic weak coupling simulations, capable of dealing with real materials in the finite-temperature formalism.

title: Modeling the amplitude and energy decay of a weakly damped harmonic oscillator using the energy dissipation rate and a simple trick
creator: Karlo Lelas, Robert Pezer
description: Abstract We demonstrate how to derive the exponential decrease of amplitude and an excellent approximation of the energy decay of a weakly damped harmonic oscillator without solving the associated equation of motion and without insight into the analytical form of its solution.

title: Multicarrier ISAC: Advances in Waveform Design, Signal Processing and Learning under Non-Idealities Thanks: V. Koivunen is with Aalto University, Finland. M. F. Keskin and H. Wymeersch are with Chalmers University of Technology, Sweden. M. Valkama is with Tampere University, Finland. N. González-Pre
creator: Visa Koivunen, Musa Furkan Keskin, Henk Wymeersch, Mikko Valkama
description: Abstract This paper addresses the topic of integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) in 5G and emerging 6G wireless networks. ISAC systems operate within shared, congested or even contested spectrum, aiming to deliver high performance in both wireless communications and radio frequency (RF) sensing. The expected benefits include more efficient utilization of spectrum, power, hardware (HW) and antenna resources.

title: A weakly monotonic, logically constrained, HORPO-variant
creator: Cynthia Kop
description: Abstract In this short paper, we present a simple variant of the recursive path ordering, specified for Logically Constrained Simply Typed Rewriting Systems (LCSTRSs). This is a method for curried systems, without λ \lambda but with partially applied function symbols, which can deal with logical constraints .

title: Exact and approximate fluxonium array modes
creator: Stephen Sorokanich, Max Hays, Neill C. Warrington
description: Abstract We present an exact solution for the linearized junction array modes of the superconducting qubit fluxonium in the absence of array disorder. This solution holds for arrays of any length and ground capacitance, and for both differential and grounded devices.

title: Convergence of Tsirelson convolution systems of probability spaces Thanks: The first author was supported by a Discovery Grant from NSERC
creator: Remus Floricel, Patrick Melanson
description: Abstract . We associate two specific projective systems of probability spaces to any Tsirelson convolution system. If the corresponding projective limit (in the sense of Bochner) exists, we say that the system is convergent in the first case and K K -convergent in the second.

title: Indefinite Causal Structure and Causal Inequalities with Time-Symmetry
creator: Luke Mrini, Lucien Hardy
description: Abstract Time–reversal symmetry is a prevalent feature of microscopic physics, including operational quantum theory and classical general relativity. Previous works have studied indefinite causal structure using the language of operational quantum theory, however, these rely on time-asymmetric conditions to constrain both operations and the process matrix.

title: APIGen: A utomated PI peline for Gen erating Verifiable and Diverse Function-Calling Datasets
creator: Zuxin Liu, Thai Hoang, Jianguo Zhang, Ming Zhu, Tian Lan, Shirley Kokane, Juntao Tan
description: Abstract The advancement of function-calling agent models requires diverse, reliable, and high-quality datasets. This paper presents APIGen, an automated data generation pipeline designed to synthesize verifiable high-quality datasets for function-calling applications. We leverage APIGen and collect 3,673 executable APIs across 21 different categories to generate diverse function-calling datasets in a scalable and structured manner.

title: Pseudo-Dirac Neutrinos and Relic Neutrino Matter Effect on the High-energy Neutrino Flavor Composition Preprint: CETUP-2023-022, FERMILAB-PUB-24-0317-T, IPPP/24/35
creator: P. S. Bhupal Dev, Pedro A. N. Machado, Ivan Martínez-Soler
description: Abstract We show that if neutrinos are pseudo-Dirac, they can potentially affect the flavor ratio predictions for the high-energy astrophysical neutrino flux observed by IceCube. In this context, we point out a novel matter effect induced by the cosmic neutrino background (C ν \nu B) on the flavor ratio composition.

title: ChronoMagic-Bench : A Benchmark for Metamorphic Evaluation of Text-to-Time-lapse Video Generation
creator: Shenghai Yuan, Jinfa Huang, Yongqi Xu, Yaoyang Liu, Shaofeng Zhang, Yujun Shi, Ruijie Zhu, Xinhua Cheng, Jiebo Luo, Li Yuan
description: Abstract We propose a novel text-to-video (T2V) generation benchmark, ChronoMagic-Bench 1 1 1 ”Chrono” derives from the Greek word ”chronos”, which means ”time”. , to evaluate the temporal and metamorphic knowledge skills in time-lapse video generation of the T2V models (e.g. Sora [ 9 ] and Lumiere [ 4 ] ).

title: A Nesterov-style Accelerated Gradient Descent Algorithm for the Symmetric Eigenvalue Problem
creator: Foivos Alimisis, Simon Vary, Bart Vandereycken
description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Foivos Alimisis, Simon Vary, Bart Vandereycken. We develop an accelerated gradient descent algorithm on the Grassmann manifold to compute the subspace spanned by a number of leading eigenvectors of a symmetric positive semi-definite matrix. This has a constant cost per iteration and a provable iteration complexity of 𝒪 ~ ​ ( 1 / δ ) \tilde{\mathcal{O}}(1/\sqrt{\delta}) , where δ \delta is the spectral gap and 𝒪 ~ \tilde{\mathcal{O}} hides logarithmic factors.

title: Playing with FIRE: A Galactic Feedback-Halting Experiment Challenges Star Formation Rate Theories
creator: Shivan Khullar, Christopher D. Matzner, Norman Murray, Michael Y. Grudić, Dávid Guszejnov, Andrew Wetzel, Philip F. Hopkins
description: Abstract Stellar feedback influences the star formation rate (SFR) and the interstellar medium of galaxies in ways that are difficult to quantify numerically, because feedback is an essential ingredient of realistic simulations. To overcome this, we conduct a feedback-halting experiment starting with a Milky Way-mass galaxy in the FIRE-2 simulation framework.

title: Two improvements in Birch’s theorem on forms Thanks: AL was supported by NSF grants DMS-2402041 and DMS-1926686. Thanks: AS was supported by NSF grant DMS-2301871.
creator: Amichai Lampert, Andrew Snowden
description: Abstract . Let K K be a Birch field , that is, a field for which every diagonal form of odd degree in sufficiently many variables admits a non-zero solution; for example, K K could be the field of rational numbers.

title: Bayesian inverse Navier–Stokes problems: joint flow field reconstruction and parameter learning
creator: Alexandros Kontogiannis †, Scott V. Elgersma, Andrew J. Sederman, Matthew P. Juniper
description: Abstract We formulate and solve a Bayesian inverse Navier–Stokes (N–S) problem that assimilates velocimetry data in order to jointly reconstruct a 3D flow field and learn the unknown N–S parameters, including the boundary position. By hardwiring a generalised N–S problem, and regularising its unknown parameters using Gaussian prior distributions, we learn the most likely parameters in a collapsed search space.

title: Feferman Interpretability We think that the class of theories realising ILM can be extended to a class of essentially sententially reflexive sequential theories . We probably need our arithmetical base to be I ​ Σ 1 \mathrm{I}\Sigma_{1} . However, this possibility has not been studied. See [ BV05 ]
creator: Joost J. Joosten, Luka Mikec, Albert Visser
description: Abstract We present an interpretability logic FIL or Feferman Interpretability Logic . The □ \Box provability modality can occur in FIL with a label, as in □ 𝔞 \Box^{\mathfrak{a}} . Likewise the ⊳ \rhd interpretability modality can occur in FIL with a label, as in ⊳ 𝔞 \rhd^{\mathfrak{a}} .

title: An Understanding of Principal Differential Analysis
creator: Edward Gunning, Giles Hooker
description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Edward Gunning, Giles Hooker. In functional data analysis, replicate observations of a smooth functional process and its derivatives offer a unique opportunity to flexibly estimate continuous-time ordinary differential equation models. Ramsay (1996a) first proposed to estimate a linear ordinary differential equation from functional data in a technique called Principal Differential Analysis, by formulating a functional regression in which the highest-order derivative of a function is modelled as a time-varying linear combination of its lower-order derivatives.

title: Complexity Aversion Thanks: I am deeply grateful to Hans Haller, Eric Bahel, Matt Kovach, and Sudipta Sarangi for their guidance and encouragement throughout this project. I would also like to thank Yaojun Liu for his suggestions. All errors in this paper are solely the responsibility of the author.
creator: Yuan Gu, Chao Hung Chan
description: Abstract . This paper proposes a model of decision-making under uncertainty in which an agent is constrained in her cognitive ability to consider complex acts. We identify the complexity of an act according to the corresponding partition of state space. The agent ranks acts according to the expected utility net of complexity cost.

title: Ground states of a nonlocal variational problem and Thomas–Fermi limit for the Choquard equation
creator: Damiano Greco, Yanghong Huang, Zeng Liu, Vitaly Moroz
description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Damiano Greco, Yanghong Huang, Zeng Liu, Vitaly Moroz. We study nonnegative optimizers of a Gagliardo–Nirenberg type inequality ∬ ℝ N × ℝ N | u ⁡ ( x ) | p ​ | u ⁡ ( y ) | p | x − y | N − α ​ 𝑑 x ​ 𝑑 y ≤ C ​ ( ∫ ℝ N | u | 2 ​ 𝑑 x ) p ​ θ ​ ( ∫ ℝ N | u | q ​ 𝑑 x
